column15: blurb
Honest steel. It asks nothing clever of you.
Slow, and it does not care.
Two cuts where one would do.
A compact ash-wood bow bound for a quick draw.
A long curve, and a long grudge.
Reach enough to keep the dead at arm's length.
Poise is a fiction. This is the argument.
Both ends are the business end.
It was a woodcutter's once.
Small enough to be quick with.
A wall you can carry. Your arm knows it.
You will not be moved. You will not move.
Plain, round, and enough.
Defence with an opinion.
Light enough to see what is coming.
Fire remembers what steel forgets.
Held wrong on purpose.
Grey wood, warm at the grip.
The stone hums before you do.
Someone knelt for this once.
It keeps a little of the guiding flame.
Cut, and still growing.
Wet to the touch. It should not be.
Blood takes to flame more readily than wood.
Taken from something that objected.
A rimed point that slows the next advance.
A furnace edge bought with a slower swing.
Its last note settles into a sheltering hush.
A wavering blade that leaves the wound open.
Thin enough to find the gap in anything.
Wide of blade, and it clears a room.
A flame-shaped blade that burns where it passes.
A duellist's point. It answers before you ask.
Stiff and four-edged, made to find the seam in plate.
Light as a promise, and kept the same way.
Cooled in ash, and it never quite cools.
Two hands, a wide stance, and no apology.
Long enough that the first blow is yours.
A harvest tool, repurposed. The crop is the same.
It takes a little back for every life it cuts.
Flanged iron and no subtlety at all.
The spikes are what it has instead of mercy.
The head has opinions about where it lands.
Built to break a stance, not a skin.
Every swing carries a little weather.
The long beard of the blade hooks what it cannot cut.
Pale along the edge, and patient as the moon.
Two crescents, and the cold follows both.
Tall as its archer, and it reaches nearly as far.
Curved to hold a draw all afternoon.
Small, spanned in a breath, and not for show.
It takes a winch to span and a wall to stop it.
It cracks from a distance and is heard from further.
Barbed cord. It bites back at the hand.
Four rings of iron, and nothing between you and the argument.
Taken from something that no longer needs them.
It hums when the sky does.
Margins crowded with someone else's fire.
Worn soft at the pages that were needed most.
A small gold disc that remembers noon.
Knuckle and thread. It listens for the dead.
